version.changelog:
- Internal skill version updated to 1.5.2.
- No file or documentation changes detected in this release.

llm.summary: The skill is not clearly malicious, but its governance and optimization features rely on missing external code and expose under-scoped security controls that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Governance checks and optimization are purpose-aligned, but loading core logic from host-relative paths and enabling session_logs in deployment guidance make behavior dependent on and broader than the packaged skill artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata declares no automatic install commands and package.json has no install script, but the guides include manual config edits, npm install, and unpinned npx ts-node benchmark commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The tools are user-invoked and mostly match the advertised domain, but security-critical scope is ambiguous: the advertised YAML veto policy is not loaded by the inspected runtime paths, optimizer examples are enabled by default, and documentation makes broad safety claims without adequate warnings.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden cron, service, or startup persistence was found; the artifact uses in-memory registries/caches and disclosed OpenClaw configuration changes that persistently enable the skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is industrial governance, veto enforcement, scoring, risk prediction, and safe optimization, but the central implementation is imported from ../../src/core/synthesizer outside the artifact and was not present in the inspected workspace; veto-check also allows caller-supplied rules to replace the default policy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Do not rely on its veto or optimizer decisions until the core synthesizer code is bundled or pinned, the active policy source is clear, caller-provided rules cannot bypass mandatory controls, and session logging or live optimization is explicitly opted in with warnings.
llm.findings:
[T08] unexpected: Supported: security-critical veto, economics, proof, risk, and optimizer logic is imported from paths outside the skill artifact, and those files were absent during inspection; documentation also uses unpinned npx ts-node for benchmarks.
[T09] unexpected: Supported: veto-check lets the same caller provide a custom rules array that replaces default governance policy, and the documented YAML veto rules are not read by the inspected enforcement paths.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly supported: several files are wrappers, benchmarks, or status/memory integrations rather than complete implementations; the larger concern is that the claimed core capabilities depend on unbundled external code.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported in documentation: credential entry, session logging, live optimization, deployment, and rollback steps are presented without adequate warnings about secrets, captured session data, or operational impact.
[RP1] unexpected: Supported but bounded: unpinned npx commands appear in documentation and may fetch code at runtime if ts-node is not installed locally; this is not automatic during skill load.
[E1] expected: The curl example posts skill metadata to the ClawHub API as part of publishing, which fits the guide's purpose, but token-handling warnings are missing.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported: multiple documents claim 100% security audit success, while the inspected audit script is pattern-based and references paths/files that are not self-contained in the artifact.
[RA2] unexpected: Not supported as scanner-stated persistence: the cited publishing text does not create cron jobs, startup scripts, or backdoors; persistent OpenClaw enablement is disclosed configuration.
[SDI-2] expected: Supported but purpose-adjacent: the agent-status module exports bulk status enumeration and registry clearing helpers; this is plausible for development/integration but under-scoped for a shared runtime.
